brief.headline: Close the ₹32.69 L annual price gap to Shrinath Roto Pack's ₹290.00/KG benchmark and capture ₹1.16 Cr working capital with 15-day faster payment against a 4.38% discount.

priceAsk.summary: Match our best laminate price of ₹290.00/KG across equivalent SKUs, closing the current 1.4-6.3% gaps on top items.
priceAsk.target: ₹32.69 L annual saving by aligning their ₹294.03-₹308.30/KG pricing to the ₹290.00/KG benchmark we already pay Shrinath Roto Pack Pvt Ltd.
priceAsk.basis: Three of their SKUs run 1.4-6.3% above our best price for comparable laminates; the ₹32.69 L excess is money we've already proven is unnecessary by paying less elsewhere.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 Days After Receipt to 15 Days After Receipt in exchange for a 2.2% price concession (half their 4.38% borrowing cost).
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Accelerating by 15 days frees ₹1.16 Cr of our working capital and saves them roughly 2.2% in interest — a win-win against their 81d cash cycle (versus 46d peer median).

brief.financialLeverage: GEEP's 1.1% net margin sits half the 2.1% peer median, and their 6.6% return on capital lags the 14.6% peer benchmark — they're operationally thin. Their 0.57x debt-to-equity and 4.12x interest coverage are stable, and the 3.35 Altman Z puts them in the safe zone, but the CRISIL BB+ / Stable rating rests on an Issuer Not Cooperating basis, so the data is stale. Our ₹28.31 Cr is 9.72% of their ₹291.36 Cr revenue — meaningful volume leverage. The slim margin and compliance red flags (GST filing delays, EPF payment delays, pending legal cases) mean we must avoid a hard squeeze that tips them into distress; instead, trade payment speed (which their 81d cycle and 4.38% borrowing cost make valuable) for price alignment.

evidence.point: We're overpaying ₹32.69 L annually versus the best laminate price we already secure.
Top SKU LM ELECTRAL MD 21.80g LS 08 costs us ₹308.30/KG — 6.3% above the ₹290.00/KG we pay Shrinath.
Our ₹28.31 Cr annual spend represents 9.72% of their ₹291.36 Cr revenue — a material customer relationship.
Their 81d cash-conversion cycle is 76% longer than the 46d peer median, so early payment is worth their 4.38% borrowing cost.
Paying 15 days earlier releases ₹1.16 Cr of our working capital.
Their 1.1% net margin is roughly half the 2.1% peer median, limiting room for deep price cuts.

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC; proven scalable second source for laminate sachets with ₹2611.64 Cr revenue and C (59/100) health.

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant (₹16492.00 Cr revenue) offering both film substrate and conversion — can second-source GEEP at scale, though health is C (46/100).

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter focused on pharma blister/sachet laminates (₹222.04 Cr revenue); strong second-source despite D (31/100) health.

risks: CRISIL BB+ / Stable rating is on an Issuer Not Cooperating basis — the financials are stale, so treat their health as uncertain and keep alternates warm.

GST filing delays, EPF payment delays, and pending legal cases signal compliance stress — pushing too hard on price could tip a 1.1% margin supplier into distress and disrupt our 67% single-source reliance.
We source 67% of our laminates (₹28.31 Cr) from GEEP alone — qualify a second converter immediately to cut supply risk and add negotiating leverage.
Their ₹-1.64 Cr negative free cash flow and 87d receivable days (versus 60d peer) mean they're cash-hungry — use payment speed as the primary lever, not margin erosion.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're carrying a ₹32.69 L annual premium versus comparable laminate prices we already pay — let's close that gap and explore faster payment terms that free up cash for both of us.
